title: WeatherNext Cyclones Gains a Full Day of Tropical Cyclone Warning Lead Time Using Coarse-Grid AI
whyItMatters: Published in Nature, WeatherNext Cyclones gained a full day of cyclone track, intensity, and size lead time—a decade of meteorological progress—using 100× coarser grids and aiding NHC’s Hurricane Melissa warning.
summary: Published in Nature on August 6, 2026 (Vol. 657, pp. 680–688, doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10953-2, PMID 42717078) alongside open-sourced weights and code, Google DeepMind, Google Research, NOAA’s National Hurricane Center (NHC), CIRA, and the UK Met Office introduced WeatherNext Cyclones (WN-C). Built on Functional Generative Networks (FGNs), WN-C generates 15-day global forecasts in under a minute on a TPU and scales to 1,000-member ensembles (vs 50 in conventional systems) to capture rare rapid-intensification tails. Evaluated across 2023–2025 global tropical cyclones, WN-C delivered an average lead-time advantage of 1 full day or more on track, intensity, and wind radius over leading operational physics models—matching an entire decade of operational meteorological progress. Strikingly, it achieved state-of-the-art intensity forecasts from 28×28 km inputs (100× coarser than regional hurricane models), overturning meteorological assumptions that kilometer-scale resolution is strictly required, and operationally helped NHC forecast Hurricane Melissa’s 2025 rapid intensification and Jamaica landfall.
technicalHighlights: Gained >= 1 full day of forecast lead time on tropical cyclone track, intensity, and wind radius over leading operational models across 2023–2025 storms—comparable to a decade of meteorological progress.
Functional Generative Networks scale operational forecasts to 1,000-member ensembles in <1 minute per member, capturing rare rapid intensification such as 2025 Hurricane Melissa.

Achieved state-of-the-art intensity skill from 28×28 km inputs (100× coarser than regional hurricane models), revealing unexpected intensity signal in coarse global fields; weights open-sourced for commercial and operational use.
caveats: Physical mechanisms explaining why coarse 28 km and even 111 km inputs support superior cyclone intensity skill remain an active open research question; deployed as consensus guidance alongside human forecasters.

scoreRationale.foundational: Challenges long-held atmospheric-physics orthodoxy by proving coarse global fields contain rich cyclone intensity information unlocked by Functional Generative Networks.
scoreRationale.ripple: Open-sourced weights and operational NHC/Met Office adoption directly translate into extra evacuation lead time and saved lives worldwide.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature and validated prospectively across 2023–2025 hurricane seasons including live operational use during Hurricane Melissa.
scoreRationale.velocity: Generates 15-day global cyclone ensembles in under one minute on a TPU, scaling to 1,000 members vs 50 in traditional numerical centers.
